method: bounded prioritised lookup; WebSearch for discovery, aii-web-tools fetch for gist, aii-web-tools fetch_grep for every quote; raw extracts in results/raw/; queries in results/search_log.md

neighbours.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
neighbours.quote: we perform directional ablation on the "refusal direction" r, ablating it from activations at all layers and all token positions
neighbours.establishes: Refusal mediated by a 1-D subspace in 13 chat models; default intervention is all-layer, all-position; weight orthogonalisation applied to every residual-stream writer.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS the placement question the all-layer default hides. STOPS: no contradiction of the all-layer result.

neighbours.title: Refusal Direction is Universal Across Safety-Aligned Languages
neighbours.quote: a vector extracted from English can bypass refusals in other languages with near-perfect effectiveness, without any additional fine-tuning
neighbours.establishes: Direction universality over 14 languages (Slovene not among them), ablation applied across all layers and token positions.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: shared direction != shared effective depth region for a bounded weight edit. STOPS: consistent with Wang at full depth.

neighbours.title: Does Localization Inform Editing? Surprising Differences in Causality-Based Localization vs. Knowledge Editing
neighbours.quote: We find that model edit success is essentially unrelated to where factual information is stored in models, as measured by Causal Tracing.
neighbours.establishes: Localisation does not predict the best layer for a weight edit; factual knowledge, ROME/MEMIT, English.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: the same shape for refusal, abliteration-style edits, and across languages, with cheap baselines named. STOPS: different measurement family.

neighbours.title: Read-Best Is Not Steer-Best: A Probing-Steering Layer Dissociation in Omni-Modal LLMs
neighbours.quote: Across three architectures the steer-best layer stays in a narrow band of normalized depth [0.48,0.74], while the probe-best layer scatters across [0.29,1.00]
neighbours.establishes: Probe-optimal != steer-optimal layer, causally tested; emotion concept; omni-modal models; single-layer activation steering; ~26-fold gap vs random-direction controls.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: effect-based selection carried into weight-edit space and conditioned on language. STOPS: no architecture-invariance claim here.

neighbours.title: Cross-Architecture Steering Transfer in Language Models
neighbours.quote: Cross-model steering vectors (B3-TI) achieve a 71.0% win rate across 15 supervised concepts versus 68.0% for same-model native vectors
neighbours.establishes: Concept directions transfer across independently trained models at >=1.7B via SAE feature alignment; scale threshold governs transfer.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: transfer failure measured on weight edits between sibling checkpoints in a second language. STOPS: no SAE alignment here.

neighbours.title: Refit the Probe: Single-Direction Ablation Is Not a Necessity Test
neighbours.quote: the layer with the highest probe accuracy is not the layer with the largest ablation response, in every pretrained model we ran, and a profile is fixed by neither measurement alone
neighbours.establishes: Readability and ablation damage peak at different depths in text LMs; single-direction ablation does not establish necessity.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: same separation for a persistent weight edit and a second language. STOPS: no INLP run here.

neighbours.title: Predicting Where Steering Vectors Succeed
neighbours.quote: peak $A_{\mathrm{lin}}$ predicts steering effectiveness at $\rho = +0.86$ to $+0.91$ and layer selection at $\rho = +0.63$ to $+0.92$
neighbours.establishes: A cheap training-free logit-lens diagnostic predicts steering effectiveness and layer choice, 24 concept families, five models, English.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: in this setting geometric predictors lose to behavioural baselines. STOPS: LAP itself was never raced here (UNEXECUTED).

neighbours.title: Signatures of Steerability in Activation Space of Language Models
neighbours.quote: simple separation metrics strongly correlate with the downstream steerability of language models across diverse settings, even after controlling for layers and dataset effects
neighbours.establishes: Cheap separability statistics predict steerability; steerability is dataset-dependent.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: separability is preserved across languages here while the edit outcome is not. STOPS: probe-based, so decodability not use.

neighbours.title: Locating and Steering Refusal Beyond Attention
neighbours.quote: even a random source direction can map to a high cosine, up to 0.515 across our pairs
neighbours.establishes: Direction cosine is unreliable as a CROSS-ARCHITECTURE transfer metric; transfer claims should rest on specificity controls, not geometry.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: cosine failing as a CROSS-LINGUAL predictor of weight-edit outcomes (rho +0.010). STOPS: no cross-model map fitted here.

neighbours.title: Not All Refusals Are Equal: How Safety Alignment Fails Cybersecurity at Scale
neighbours.quote: we opted for uniformly spread layer selection across 25-95% of model depth, which we found to substantially outperform norm-based selection (targeting layers with the highest refusal signal norm) by up to ~70pp of additional refusal reduction
neighbours.establishes: Refusal distributed widely across layers in modern models; uniform layer spread beats signal-norm-based selection across 24 models; also the source of the '2-3 middle layers' attribution to Arditi et al.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: matched-energy, matched-count, per-language placement contrast. STOPS: the ~70pp figure is English-only and not replicated here. See results/unverified_claims.md.

neighbours.title: No Single Neuron of Failure: Distributed Safety Alignment Against White-Box Attacks
neighbours.quote: we propose distributed safety alignment (DSA), which redundantly encodes safety capabilities across multiple computational neurons
neighbours.establishes: Safety can be trained to be redundantly distributed; a training-time defence.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: descriptive depth localisation in shipped checkpoints, per language. STOPS: no training here.

neighbours.title: Localizing Safety Alignment: MLP Layers and Mid-Network Blocks Encode Refusal Behavior
neighbours.quote: in five of six greedy trajectories, adding more aligned blocks can reduce refusal performance
neighbours.establishes: Weight-space localisation of refusal to mid-network MLP blocks (layers 8-11 first in all six greedy searches); composition is non-additive.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: Closest parallel to 'concentrating beats spreading at matched energy'. ADDS: energy- and count-matched contrasts, second language. STOPS: transplantation != projection.

neighbours.title: Decided Upstream, Written Late: Locating and Pricing the Cross-Lingual Refusal Circuit of a Multilingual MoE
neighbours.quote: Harm is encoded as an internal direction that is nearly language-invariant in mid-network (English-vs-Indic cosine 0.9 at L11)
neighbours.establishes: Detection is shared and mid-network; the refusal write is late and orthogonal; harm-expert overlap between Indic languages and English peaks at Jaccard 0.43 at L11 and collapses to 0.027 at L18.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: Independent support for shared detection / language-specific execution. ADDS: persistent weight edit, matched-energy placement. STOPS: no MoE, no routing analysis.

neighbours.title: A StrongREJECT for Empty Jailbreaks
neighbours.quote: Most of the baseline automated evaluators overestimate how effective jailbreak methods are on average, especially string matching for non-refusal.
neighbours.establishes: Substring/non-refusal metrics overstate jailbreak success at evaluation time; string matching is the most biased evaluator tested.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: the same defect inside an optimiser's objective = a SELECTION failure. STOPS: refusal class only, no specificity/convincingness scoring here.

neighbours.title: XSTest: A Test Suite for Identifying Exaggerated Safety Behaviours
neighbours.quote: Partial Refusal is any combination of refusal and compliance.
neighbours.establishes: Partial compliance as a first-class annotation class alongside full compliance and full refusal.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: PARTIAL as a dose-dependent quantity inside an edit sweep. STOPS: XSTest classes are human-annotated; ours are automatic with native review pending.

neighbours.title: Validity-Aware Jailbreak Evaluation for Large Language Models
neighbours.quote: reclassifies 22.1%--51.0% of sampled prior-labeled successes as invalid across three of four public benchmarks
neighbours.establishes: Validity/correctness checking overturns a large share of previously successful jailbreak labels.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: an explicit INVALID class per cell plus wrong-language checks. STOPS: no factual-correctness verification here.

neighbours.title: AdvPrefix: An Objective for Nuanced LLM Jailbreaks
neighbours.quote: Misspecified: even with low optimization loss, actual responses are often incomplete or unfaithful
neighbours.establishes: A misspecified objective inside an optimiser yields low loss without the intended behaviour; repairing it changes what the search finds (GCG on Llama-3: 14% -> 80%).
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: CLOSEST neighbour for the selection-side point. ADDS: the weight-edit instance, quantified as a blind fraction of the search's own candidates, cross-lingually asymmetric. STOPS: the general point is AdvPrefix's.

neighbours.title: How Reliable Is Your Jailbreak Judge? Calibration and Adversarial Robustness of Automated ASR Scoring
neighbours.quote: Wrappers that leave the harmful text untouched and only add benign framing flip every LLM-judge between 57% and 100% of the time
neighbours.establishes: Automated ASR judges disagree with humans and each other and are attackable; recommends reporting judge precision/recall on a human-labelled slice.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: Supports judge-sensitivity reporting here. STOPS: our judge is validated against a frontier-model subsample, not human labels.

neighbours.title: How Does Quantization Affect Multilingual LLMs?
neighbours.quote: a 1.7% average drop in Japanese across automatic tasks corresponds to a 16.0% drop reported by human evaluators on realistic prompts
neighbours.establishes: Automatic metrics severely underestimate quantisation damage in non-English relative to human evaluation.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: Bounds the 'utility preserved' reading: NF4 throughout, automatic metrics only. STOPS: no human utility evaluation here.

neighbours.title: Who Pays More for Safety? Measuring the Disparate Cost of Safety Alignment across Languages
neighbours.quote: we instantiate Munalg using a safety-ablated (abliterated) version of the models
neighbours.establishes: Abliterated checkpoints used as the unaligned counterfactual for measuring safety cost across languages; non-English users bear a higher cost.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: evidence that an English-selected edit does not reach the same state in every language, so the counterfactual is language-dependent. STOPS: n=2 siblings, one non-English language in matched panels.

neighbours.title: Multilingual Refusal Alignment for Safer Large Language Models (RefusEU)
neighbours.quote: To collect unsafe answers, we use an abliterated version of Llama-3.1-70B, named Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-lorablated
neighbours.establishes: Source of this run's official EN/SL evaluation data; second instance of abliteration as an unaligned reference.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: measurement of four checkpoints under RefusEU in both languages. STOPS: EN/SL rows sharing a row_id are not translations, so paired claims use S5X only.

neighbours.title: Multilingual Safety Signals Are Multi-Layered: Filtering Safety-Degrading Data for Safer LLMs
neighbours.quote: sensitive layers are only partially shared across languages, with safety-relevant signals often distributed across multiple layers
neighbours.establishes: Language-specific safety-sensitive DEPTHS, 18 languages, 36K queries; used for fine-tuning-data filtering.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: The neighbour that shrinks this run's delta: language-dependent safety depth is prior work. ADDS: the consequence for weight-edit placement at matched energy and count.

neighbours.title: Multilingual Steering by Design: Multilingual Sparse Autoencoders and Principled Layer Selection
neighbours.quote: we introduce an a priori steering layer-selection rule based on the intersection of multilingual alignment and language separability, which predicts effective intervention depths without exhaustive layerwise search
neighbours.establishes: A language-aware a priori layer-selection rule exists for SAE-based language control (MT, cross-lingual summarisation), not for safety.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: selection by measured causal effect on refusal in weight-edit space, and a reported FAILURE against trivial baselines. STOPS: this rule was never raced here (UNEXECUTED).

neighbours.title: The Illusion of Cross-Lingual Safety in Low-Resource Languages
neighbours.quote: harmful prompts retain less than 10% of the English refusal signal across most language-model pairs
neighbours.establishes: Main published counterweight to direction universality; four African languages; semantic alignment preserved but layer-wise drift.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: Places this run between N2 and N24. STOPS: Slovene is mid-resource; one non-English language in matched panels.

neighbours.title: Low-Resource Safety Failures Are Action Failures, Not Representation Failures
neighbours.quote: The relevant representation is present. Yet harmful refusal drops from 87.9% to 43.9%.
neighbours.establishes: Representation vs action separation for cross-lingual safety, with a recalibration repair using 1-4 examples per class.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: ADDS: the same separation on the REMOVAL side. STOPS: no repair attempted here.

neighbours.title: Does Fine-Tuning Undo Activation Steering? Behavioural Recovery Without Weight-Edit Reversal
neighbours.quote: the weight edit survives almost untouched even where behaviour reverts: mean vector recovery is $\rho = 0.004$
neighbours.establishes: A published geometry/behaviour dissociation for weight-embedded steering: geometry intact, behaviour gone.
neighbours.delta_and_stopping_point: Nearest neighbour for 'geometry does not tell you the behavioural outcome of a weight edit'. ADDS: the predictive, cross-lingual version. STOPS: no fine-tuning here.
